entries.title: Remember has a new Explore conversation
entries.body: Remember has a new choice, Explore, beside Recall, Tutorial and Quiz. It is a conversation for thinking an article through and applying it to your own cases. It can draw on the notes, highlights and conversations you already have on the article, and it can search the web to set the piece in the wider world. You type or dictate; it is not a spoken conversation. Each article has one Explore conversation.

entries.title: Chat can look at your notes and highlights
entries.body: When you ask Chat about an article, it can look up the comments, highlights and bookmarks you have made on it, see a list of your other conversations about it, and read one of them. So you can ask about something you marked or discussed earlier without repeating it. A long set of notes is shortened, but the counts it gives are exact.

entries.title: Comment box gets Discard, Ask AI and Save
entries.body: The box that opens when you select text has Discard, Ask AI and Save buttons in place of the AI tick-box. Ask AI saves your comment and opens Chat with it filled in, for you to send. If you close the box or leave the page with something in it, the app tries to save it rather than dropping it.

entries.title: Citations say when a work's influence is unknown
entries.body: Newly made citation lists mark a work 'influence unknown' when the AI is not confident of its standing, rather than giving it a low score. On your own articles, Dig deeper may add an estimate of influence from the web, shown with its source; most searches find nothing usable. Older lists keep their scores until regenerated.

entries.title: Quick search falls back to looser matches
entries.body: When Quick search finds no passage that matches closely, it shows the best looser matches instead of an empty result. A search for a single word could come back with nothing even though relevant passages were there. If nothing matches even loosely, the result is still empty.

entries.title: Glossaries leave out works that are only cited
entries.body: New glossaries are built to leave out papers and authors an article merely cites; those belong in Citations. People and works the article discusses in their own right are still included. This applies when a glossary is made or regenerated; existing glossaries are not rewritten.

entries.title: Adding an article retries after a dropped connection
entries.body: A brief connection failure to the AI service while an article was being added could make the whole thing fail. The app tries that step again a limited number of times before giving up.

entries.title: An app left open reloads after an update
entries.body: If you kept Spideryarn open, or opened it from a home-screen icon, a page could fail with “Part of Spideryarn didn’t arrive” after we updated the app. The app checks whether a newer version is live and reloads itself; if it still cannot load the page, the message has a Reload button.
